steps.title: Welcome
steps.body: A short setup to get this app ready. Nothing here is required; you can close it and come back later.

steps.title: Load example data?
steps.body: Example data fills the lists, detail pages and dashboards so you can see the app working straight away. Pick "None" on a production install.

steps.title: Load the example data
steps.body: Loads what you picked. The data is obviously sample data, it is safe to run more than once, and you can delete it afterwards.

store._note: Configuration exchange, not rows. A configuration set carries the registers, schemas, objects, views, flows, sources and mappings that make one way of working hold together. There is deliberately NO `installable` allowlist: a set exists to introduce schemas the instance does not have YET, so listing schemas this app already owns would refuse exactly the sets worth installing. The trust boundary for a bundle is its publisher, enforced by the engine's source allowlist and trusted-key check. ⚠️ An EMPTY `installable` means install NOTHING, not install anything — omitting the key and declaring an empty list are different things.

pages.title: Store

config.title: Store
config.description: Install portal configurations that other organisations have published: a theme, a set of pages, or the flows behind a form.

pages._note: ADR-114 Decision 4 / ADR-080. Declarative: openregister hosts the store plane, so this app writes NO store controller. With no registry configured the page renders the app's built-in items and makes NO network call.

pages.title: Reports

config.description: Pick a report to open it.

cards.label: Traffic
cards.description: How much your portals are used, and by whom.

pages._note: ADR-112 / ADR-114 Decision 3. Portaliq already had one report and it was a main-nav entry at order 50. Nothing is invented here: the Traffic page is untouched and stays routable at /traffic, and only its menu entry moves, becoming a card. Themes is NOT carded — it is configuration for how a portal looks, not a reading of what happened, and ADR-097 keeps a domain of the work in the main nav.

pages.title: Traffic

config.description: What visitors looked at, who they were, where they came from and whether they did what the portal hoped. Pick a portal, a period and a segment at the top; the numbers come from the daily figures the aggregation job writes every fifteen minutes, and Export downloads exactly what the page shows.

pages._note: portal-traffic-analytics. The three stats-blocks this page used to carry counted portalSession, revoked portalSession and portalMessage rows: authenticated-session bookkeeping that said nothing about visitors (task 0.1). The six widgets here read portalTrafficDaily through the object API and say 'not measured' for a portal with measurement off instead of drawing a zero. portal-traffic-visitors-and-geo added the period selector (on the overview, read by every widget through the report store) and the Visitors widget. portal-traffic-outcomes added Goals, Funnels, Forms and Custom dimensions, the missing pages under Pages and the searches under Sources. portal-traffic-reporting added the segment selector and the Export button on the overview, the roll-up note, and the Script errors widget. The Export is a button on the overview widget rather than a manifest headerAction: nc-vue's dashboard header actions cannot read the portal, period and segment the page has selected, and a download of the wrong selection is worse than none. portal-traffic-experiments added Experiments, Heatmap and Session recordings; the last two say "off for this portal" unless the operator accepted the switch's warning. portal-traffic-kpi-cards moved the four headline numbers out of the overview into four TrafficKpi cards below it. They follow the overview's portal, period and segment and carry no picker of their own: the page has one period. The page selects the portal named in ?portal=, which is how a portal page's KPI cards link here.

config._note: Identity/access-holder archetype: a portalAccount links one external IdP identity (eHerkenning/DigiD/eIDAS) to the subjectRef domain apps scope data by, so its detail page answers 'who is this and what sessions have they used to access the portal'. ADR-062 rev3 update: the summaryAggregates header chips are retired in favour of an in-grid stats-block card (account-stats) placed top-right of the lead account-data widget, both sized h5 so the row closes together; account-sessions moves below as its own full-width row. account-sessions gets allowCreate:false — sessions are IdP-minted at login time, never hand-created — plus a viewAllRoute to the fleet-wide PortalSessions index (the only session-listing page; no per-account filtered page exists) with a token-resolved viewAllQuery so the link at least carries the account's id. CORRECTION (measured): every filter on this page addressed `accountRef`, a property NO portalSession carries — the objects link to their account by `subjectRef`. A filter naming a property the rows do not have matches nothing and reports it as an honest zero, so the two session stats read 0 and the session list read 'No sessions issued yet' for every account, always, while looking perfectly configured. Now filtered on `subjectRef: @object.subjectRef`. Verified against the API before and after: `?accountRef=<id>` returned 0 of 100 sessions, `?subjectRef=e2e-smoke` returned 3 — the positive control that proves the mechanism works and the property was the fault. The same correction admits the messages list this note previously ruled out: subjectRef is not an object id, so `@objectId` indeed cannot filter it, but `@object.<field>` can and does (2 messages for dev-supplier). No Related panel: portalAccount declares no object-reference properties of its own (organisation is a plain tenant string, not an OR ref). CORRECTION (leaf-integrations): the calendar leaf is now adopted. The earlier note ruled out every leaf on the grounds that an auth-edge identity record bears no documents, which holds for files and contacts and still does, but an appointment is not a document: staff had sessions and messages for this subject and nowhere to see or plan a meeting with them. The Meetings leaf renders in the Nextcloud shell only (ADR-046); any visitor-facing appointment view must be portal-rendered from OpenRegister objects and never embed or link the Calendar app. Still no files/contacts leaves. status is a genuine two-state lifecycle (active/suspended) so lifecycleActions is wired to it. Audit history stays a sidebar tab.

Security-token archetype: a portalSession is a bearer session minted for one portalAccount, so what matters when opening it is 'who does this belong to, what trust level, is it still valid'. The body leads with the session's own fields (audience, organisation, jti, trustLevel, issuedAt, expiresAt, revoked) in an 8-wide data card beside a 4-wide Related panel that resolves the accountRef FK back to the issuing portalAccount — the schema's only outbound object reference, now expressed as a canonical $ref+format:uuid property (ADR-062 rule 7) so the Related panel can resolve it to a display name instead of a raw uuid. No child object-list: nothing in this register points AT a portalSession. No files/calendar/contacts/talk leaves: a session is a pure auth-edge token, not content-bearing. No lifecycleActions: revoked is a one-way flag flipped by logout/admin action, not a modeled multi-state lifecycle. Audit history stays a sidebar tab.

Inbox-item archetype: a portalMessage is a single notification delivered to a subject's portal inbox, so the whole record is small enough to read at a glance — the body is one full-width data card with all fields (subject, body, read, receivedAt, subjectRef, organisation). No Related panel: subjectRef is the plain pseudonymous identity string the IdP/domain app returned, NOT an OR object reference (portalMessage has no accountRef FK), so there is nothing to resolve. No child object-list: nothing in this register points at a portalMessage. CORRECTION (leaf-integrations): the talk leaf is now adopted. The earlier note reasoned about the message as a document and concluded it carried nothing to chat about, but the thing staff need a conversation for is not the text, it is the answer: two employees deciding how to reply to a citizen did that in an unlinked room or in email, off the record. The talk leaf attaches that conversation to the message object, on the internal side only (ADR-046): the citizen's half of the exchange stays a portalMessage served through the portal edge, and no join link is ever written into an edge-served field. Still no files/contacts leaves, for the original reason. No lifecycleActions: read is a one-way flag toggled by the portal UI, not a modeled lifecycle. Audit history stays a sidebar tab.

Proof-of-receipt archetype, following the PortalMessages / PortalMessageDetail pair. The schema has carried the WMEBV burden of proof since the receipts change and had no page at all: staff triaging a failed delivery read the database or nothing. The index projects the facts a triage list needs (appId, actionId, submittedAt, deliveryStatus as a badge) and deliberately leaves payloadCopy off, because payloadCopy is whatever a citizen typed and a list renders many rows at once; it belongs on the detail page, where reading one record is the intent. Adding these pages changes who RENDERS the record, not who may read it: access stays OpenRegister RBAC exactly as for account-messages. The forms leaf sits beside the data card so a handler can link the Nextcloud Form behind a submission or a follow-up form to it. That leaf is internal-only (ADR-046): the visitor's form experience is the portal edge's own submission flow and its receipt message, and a portal visitor is never shown or invited into the Forms app. No lifecycleActions: deliveryStatus is a retriability signal the receipt service writes, not a lifecycle a person drives. Audit history stays a sidebar tab.

A portal's menus, pages and glossary live HERE rather than as their own top-level navigation entries: they are not free-standing collections, they are what one portal is made of, and a fleet-wide list of 'all pages' answers no question an editor actually has. They are `object-list` widgets filtered on `portal: @object.slug` — the token resolves against the portal being viewed. NOT `@objectId`: these children reference their portal by SLUG, not by object id, and a filter naming a property the rows do not carry matches nothing and says nothing (see PortalAccountDetail, where exactly that went unnoticed). Each filter was run against the API before being written here: 7 pages, 1 menu, 2 glossary terms for open-tilburg. portal-traffic-kpi-cards: four traffic KPI cards head the page (page views, sessions, visitors, engaged sessions), the same four numbers the Traffic page shows. Each is a PortalTrafficKpi around nc-vue's CnStatWidget with its own period picker; the 30-day preset has the id '' so the picker opens on it, and the summary endpoint reads an empty period as 30. A card opens the Traffic page with this portal selected. A portal with measurement off reads 'Not measured' and asks for nothing.

config._note: portal-page-traffic: four traffic KPI cards head the page (page views, sessions, visitors, engaged sessions) for this one page, then the page details, then Incoming and Outgoing traffic side by side. The cards are the portal page's PortalTrafficKpi with scope 'page': they read GET /api/traffic/page with the page's `portal` slug and `route`, each with its own period picker, and open the Traffic page with the portal selected. A page is matched to its traffic by its route within its portal; see openspec/changes/portal-page-traffic/proposal.md. Adding widgets replaces the default detail body, so the page details are a `data` widget here, as on PortalDetail.

pages.title: Page layout
pages._note: A page body is a widget grid on the shared 12-column geometry, and no built-in page type edits one: the detail page renders the object as fields, which for body.widgets means an array of grid integers in a textarea. This custom page places, moves and resizes those widgets directly, and is what the floating editing control on the site links to.

pages.title: Flows
pages._note: ADR-110 Decision 4: a flow is app-specific, so the authoring surface lives here rather than behind a deep link to another app's list. An ordinary index over the named `flows` source (config.entitySource) rather than the deprecated `flows` page type, reading OpenRegister's one native flow store (ADR-065), scoped to this app by config.app.

pages.title: Flow
pages._note: The shared CnFlowDetail canvas over the same single engine. Controls render in the NC app sidebar (sidebarComponent) so the canvas keeps full width, and the canvas and the sidebar share useFlowStore.

pages.title: Integrations
pages._note: adopt-connection-registry (hydra connection-registry D8, hydra#667, #673, #674 and #676). The rows are integriq's `app_connection` objects, synced from lib/Settings/connections.json; integriq works out each status. The app=portaliq preset is the IntegrationsMenu entry's `query` (ADR-097 decision 5), which the index page merges into the fetch as a bare filter key. `showAdd` is false because a row nothing declared has nothing to check (D9). Add integration leaves for integriq's overview through the openIntegriqConnections handler in src/customComponents.js, because a header action's `navigate` only pushes a route inside this app.

steps.title: Welcome to Portaliq
steps.body: A short tour of the main screens. It takes under a minute, and you can close it at any point and pick it up again from the help menu.
Flows automate the repetitive parts of this app. They live behind the Settings button at the bottom of the menu. Have a look, though you do not have to build one now.
steps.task: Open Settings at the bottom of the menu, then Flows
